answer: Plume-Wharf Commit Registry: agents register by submitting a hardware-attested nonce derived from a per-epoch wharf beacon, and each registration must include a freshly solved, verifier-unique challenge bound to that nonce plus the agent's first Haven transaction hash. Duplicate nonces or reused challenge solutions are rejected at the registry, so copying a valid answer yields nothing. Cost to an attacker: one distinct hardware root and unique on-chain Haven seed per identity, making N identities cost N real devices and N seed transactions, not one replayable proof.
